issues.description: The problem statement/UML specifies a top-level class named `Farm`, but the template file `src/de/tum/cit/ase/Farm.java` declares `public class AnimalFarm`. Students following the statement will implement/refer to `Farm`, while the starter code suggests `AnimalFarm`, causing name mismatches with provided examples and the intended design.
issues.suggestedFix: Update the template `src/de/tum/cit/ase/Farm.java` to declare `public class Farm` (matching the UML/problem statement) and ensure any references/comments in the template align with `Farm`.

issues.description: The template `src/de/tum/cit/ase/Farm.java` defines `singFarmSongVerse` with no parameters (commented as `/*Animal animal*/`), while the UML/problem statement and the solution require `singFarmSongVerse(Animal animal)`. This prevents students from implementing the required verse logic per animal using the provided stub signature.
issues.suggestedFix: Change the template method signature to `private void singFarmSongVerse(Animal animal)` and add/import the `Animal` type as needed.

issues.description: The template `src/de/tum/cit/ase/Farm.java` contains an invalid nested duplicate declaration: inside `singFarmSong()` it repeats `package de.tum.cit.ase;` and declares another `public class AnimalFarm`. This makes the starter code uncompilable, blocking students from running or extending the template.
issues.suggestedFix: Remove the duplicated `package` statement and the inner `public class AnimalFarm` block from within `singFarmSong()`, leaving exactly one top-level package declaration and one top-level class per file.
